Latin word

jugum

jugum, jugī n.

noun, second declension

a ridge, the crest of a hill; a ridge; a chain of mountains; ridge or pass; a yoke for oxen

In this lexicon

  • crest

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 299

  • mountain range

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short: “a height or summit of a mountain, a ridge; also, a chain of mountains” (Verg. E. 5.76; Caes. BC 1.70); M-O s.v. mountain range or chain; Traupman 202: Alpium juga, the Alpine chain

  • ridge

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 204–206; Traupman 203

  • yoke

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. ND 2.151: nōs onera quibusdam bēstiīs, nōs juga impōnimus (Lewis & Short); Verg. G. 3.57: juga dētractāns (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • aspice, arātra jugō referunt suspēnsa juvencī

    look, the bullocks are bringing home the ploughs hung from the yokeVerg. E. 2.66

    In the entry for yoke

  • rōbustus quoque jam taurīs juga solvet arātor

    the sturdy ploughman too will now take the yoke off his bullsVerg. E. 4.41

    In the entry for yoke
